input.description: Read flatline code_review config and adversarial-review.sh flag support

content.content:
flatline_protocol:
  enabled: true
  auto_trigger: true
  phases:
    prd: true
    sdd: true
    sprint: true
  models:
    # 2026-10-01: claude-headless = Fable 5.1 on the CLI/Bedrock; `opus`/`fable` are http_api ids that fail
    # INVALID_CONFIG without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (fleet-measured, search 2026-10-01). Was opus.
    # Flatline runs its voices in parallel and nothing serialises CLI hops across it (the per-binary lock is
    # adversarial-review.sh's): two claude -p calls share the CLI and the plan window, each bounded by the catalog's
    # headless_timeout_seconds (900 s) — up to ~15 min per phase under contention (KF-037 / KF-038).
    # Its auth follows CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (the claude-bedrock wrapper for Bedrock, else the plain CLI's own login — bd-swz7), and it
    # shares the anthropic headless circuit breaker with the dissent companion: a rate limit on either opens it for both.
    # (thirty-seventh run, e2b DISS-C-002) so a Flatline rate limit leaves a review that follows while the breaker is open
    # single-voice: its companion is refused by the open breaker, the envelope reads companion_voice.status failed (not degraded),
    # and nothing in the unattended harness re-runs it (KF-038) — read companion_voice before taking such a review as two-voice.
    # (thirty-ninth run, e2b DISS-C-002/003) the route — and the account billed — is the environment's, not this file's: a shell
    # without CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (cron, CI, a fresh login) runs Flatline and Bridgebuilder on the plain CLI's plan, and the breaker
    # bucket is anthropic/headless whatever the route, so a plan-window limit there also refuses a Bedrock-wrapped companion; export
    # the wrapper in every shell that runs them, and clear a bucket opened on the other route with `cheval --reset-breaker anthropic:headless`.
    primary: claude-headless
    # cycle-109 substrate-debug (2026-05-13): switched secondary from gpt-5.5-pro
    # to gpt-5.5 (non-pro). Direct probe of current OpenAI key showed it lacks
    # Pro-tier access (gpt-5.5-pro → 404 "not a chat model" on /v1/chat/completions
    # AND insufficient_quota on /v1/responses; gpt-5.5 → success with correct
    # params). gpt-5.5 is the cost-safe default per cycle-095 Sprint 2; alias
    # already in substrate catalog. Filed as cycle-109 evidence (C109.OP-6):
    # substrate misdiagnosed model-tier-access-denied as insufficient_quota —
    # FR-1 capability-aware substrate would have caught this at boot.
    secondary: gpt-5.5
    # cycle-124 (2026-09-17): tertiary DISABLED on this host — gemini CLI is tier-blocked (KF-018, rec 2) and
    # hounfour.headless.mode cli-only never reaches the HTTP rung, so a configured tertiary only turns every
    # Flatline run into 2/3 DEGRADED (Phase 2 skipped). Fleet baseline (framework-review §10): no tertiary
    # unless `agy` is installed. Re-enable by restoring the line below.
    # tertiary: gemini-3.1-pro # cheval bare-alias (resolves to API id gemini-3.1-pro-preview); was gemini-3.1-pro-preview which is not a valid cheval alias — see cycle-102 flatline-prd-degradation.md
  thresholds:
    high_consensus: 700
    disputed_delta: 300
    low_value: 400
    blocker_skeptic: 700
  max_iterations: 5
  # Phase 2.5: Adversarial cross-model review (PR #552 enforcement gate)
  # When enabled, `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint` invoke a cross-model
  # dissenter (gpt-5.3-codex by default) and produce adversarial-{review,audit}.json.
  # The PreToolUse:Write hook at .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
  # blocks COMPLETED marker writes when enabled but the artifact is missing.
  # Emergency override: LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false.
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    # cycle-104 Sprint 2 T2.9 (2026-05-12): REVERTED to gpt-5.5-pro per
    # SDD R8. Closing evidence:
    #   (1) Architecture proof — chain_resolver populates the within-
    #       company chain `gpt-5.5-pro → gpt-5.5 → gpt-5.3-codex → codex-headless`
    #       and cheval.cmd_invoke walks it on EmptyContentError. Pinned by
    #       .claude/adapters/tests/test_chain_walk_audit_envelope.py
    #       (test_primary_empty_content_walks_to_fallback mocks the
    #       primary returning EMPTY_CONTENT and asserts walk to fallback).
    #   (2) Empirical evidence — cycle-104 sprint-2 T2.10 25-trial live
    #       replay (2026-05-12) showed KF-003 NOT REPRODUCIBLE at OpenAI
    #       across 5 sizes × 5 prompts at 30K-80K input tokens.
    # The T1B.4 workaround is no longer load-bearing. If KF-003 returns,
    # the chain absorbs it; if the chain exhausts, T2.8 voice-drop keeps
    # consensus available with the remaining voices. gpt-5.5-pro restores
    # cross-model dissent diversity per cycle-102 §G2 rationale.
    # Original cycle-102 T1B.4 swap comment retained in git history.
    model: gpt-5.5-pro
    budget_cents: 200
    timeout_seconds: 600
    # KF-011 sub-mode (c) mitigation (2026-05-17): Gemini-3.1-pro empty-content
    # on review-type prompts post cycle-109 T4.10. Adding claude-headless as a
    # 4th-line voice so quorum is reachable when Gemini is silent. KF-011
    # sub-mode (b) resolved by parser fix in d9ec8cb5; this entry covers (c).
    fallback_chain:

1074	def remove_colliding(t, tree):
1075	    """1.2.11: a .py file at a path that is neither a hidden overlay dest nor present in the fixture, whose basename
1076	    equals the basename of a hidden overlay .py file or of a fixture .py file under tests/ or test/, is removed: under
1077	    the default import mode pytest imports package-less test modules by basename and a second module with the same
1078	    basename aborts collection. Paths go to grading/<label>.colliding-removed.txt beside the tree → count"""
1079	    owned = {d for _s, d, f in t.overlay if not os.path.isdir(f)}
1080	    owned_dirs = tuple(d + "/" for _s, d, f in t.overlay if os.path.isdir(f))
1081	    reserved = {d.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for d in owned if d.endswith(".py")}
1082	    fx = t.fixture or ""
1083	    if fx and os.path.isdir(fx):
1084	        for r, _ds, fs in os.walk(fx, followlinks=False):
1085	            parts = os.path.relpath(r, fx).replace(os.sep, "/").split("/")
1086	            if any(p in ("tests", "test") for p in parts):
1087	                reserved.update(n for n in fs if n.endswith(".py") and n not in ("__init__.py", "conftest.py"))
1088	    reserved.discard("conftest.py")   # pytest registers conftest modules per directory; remove_harness owns them
1089	    found = []
1090	    for r, ds, fs in os.walk(tree, followlinks=False):
1091	        relr = os.path.relpath(r, tree)
1092	        for name in sorted(fs):
1093	            if name not in reserved:
1094	                continue
1095	            rel = name if relr == "." else relr.replace(os.sep, "/") + "/" + name
1096	            if rel in owned or rel.startswith(owned_dirs) or (fx and os.path.lexists(os.path.join(fx, *rel.split("/")))):
1097	                continue
1098	            found.append((rel, os.path.join(r, name)))
1099	    for _rel, p in found:
1100	        os.unlink(p)
1101	    with open(tree.rstrip("/") + ".colliding-removed.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
1102	        f.write("".join(rel + "\n" for rel, _p in sorted(found)))
1103	    return len(found)
1104	
1105

Scope: pr/head.diff (12 files: evals/harness/{ablation-grade.sh,lib/arms-common.sh,pipeline-run.sh,run-ablation.sh}, evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml, evals/tests/*.bats, evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-pipeline-stub.sh).

1. ablation-grade.sh remove_colliding (head lines 1074-1103). `reserved` is built from EVERY `.py` basename under the fixture's tests/ or test/ directories (line 1087) and every hidden-overlay `.py` dest basename (line 1081), not only pytest-collectable test modules (test_*.py / *_test.py). The grader's own 1.2.11 note (line 221) says fixture suites rely on sibling modules like `helpers.py` / `_oracle_x.py`. An agent that adds `src/<pkg>/helpers.py` (or `utils.py`, `common.py`, or `__init__.py` when an overlay dest is one) as part of a correct solution has that file unlinked from the grading tree before any command runs (lines 1090-1100) -> ImportError -> a correct solution graded as failing. 2. Same function: no check for `__init__.py` in the agent file's directory. Under pytest prepend import mode a module inside a package is imported as `pkg.test_slug`, which does not collide with a package-less `tests/test_slug.py`; the docstring says "package-less directories" but the code removes package modules too. Agent tests silently disappear from hidden_tests.total.
3. COLLIDING[0] accumulates across every prepare() call (final, base, implement, fix1 snapshots), so `colliding_tests_removed` is a multiple of the real file count when snapshots are graded. Mirrors harness_files_removed; semantics worth confirming.
4. run-ablation.sh codex pre-flight (lines 784-840): `uses_codex` treats every arm without `toggles.loa_mount: false` as codex-using, including a4_no_gates (phases PLAN, IMPLEMENT only; never runs the dissent) -> an a4-only batch is refused on an expired token unnecessarily (fail-closed, documented as "every arm except one whose toggles set loa_mount: false"). Any failure mode where `tokens` is not a dict or refresh_token absent is a silent pass-through (mirrors host). Confirm nothing else leaks token material to argv/logs.

Not verifiable from the PR files.

8. The --types jq fix (run-ablation.sh line 565) looks correct: `.type as $t | (... | index($t))`.

The walk at lines 1090-1100 then unlinks any file with a reserved basename anywhere in the agent's tree that is not an overlay dest and not present in the fixture. Concrete input: fixture has \`tests/helpers.py\` (the pattern the 1.2.11 note itself cites); the agent's correct solution adds \`src/<pkg>/helpers.py\`; the file is deleted before \`test_command\` runs; the hidden tests import the package, hit ImportError, and the trial is rowed as failing with its cost spent. Nothing surfaces except a line in \`grading/<label>.colliding-removed.txt\`.
**File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081\`, \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1087\`, \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1090-1100\`

...
reserved.update(n for n in fs if TEST_MOD.match(n))

(DISS-C-003)
**Suggestion:** Skip files whose directory, or any ancestor up to the tree root, contains \`__init__.py\`.

### 2. Grader — directory overlays are not covered by the fix

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081\` — only file-destination overlays feed \`reserved\`; an overlay whose source is a directory is recorded in \`owned_dirs\` (line 1080) and its inner \`.py\` files are never reserved. (DISS-C-002)
**Suggestion:** Walk directory overlays and add their collectable test-module basenames to \`reserved\`.
**Benefit:** The 1.2.11 guarantee holds for every overlay shape \`put_file\` accepts.

### 3. Codex pre-flight — the horizon and the arm set over-approximate

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) \`head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:806\` — \`required\` is now + 2 × Σ watchdog_s / concurrency, but \`watchdog_s\` is already twice the phase-sum timeout (RAB-1's comment at \`head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:93\`), so the horizon is four times the phase sum per trial and, on \`--resume\`, counts trials already rowed. Line 792 (\`uses_codex\`) also counts \`a4_no_gates\` (phases PLAN, IMPLEMENT; no dissent) as codex-using, so an a4-only batch is refused for a credential it never uses. Fail-closed, and documented at lines 110-120, so not blocking. (DISS-C-005)

**Benefit:** Legitimate batches and resumes are not refused; the pre-flight still catches the KF-048 case.
